title: Job application automation
description: Tired of manually tracking hundreds of job applications, I built a management system with a UI-widget and a SQLite database. The user can filter their applications, mark the current stage (applied/interviewed/accepted/rejected) and more. I also connected it to an API that automatically scrapes the internet for relevant job listings.

title: Brain tumour classification using Deep Learning
description: In my Master's thesis I classified diagnosis and location of tumours by fine-tuning pre-trained ResNet and VisionTransformer models on MRI sequence combinations.

title: Personal website
description: I designed and built this website myself.

title: Visualisations of sorting algorithms
description: I implemented a couple of sorting algorithms, and created a visualisation of them, available on this very site!

title: Work Clock
description: A timer widget that saves work-session data in a SQLite database, and automatically generates plots for immediate insight.

title: Initialization of k-means
description: In my Bachelor's thesis I investigated three initialization methods for the k-means algorithm.

title: Knapsack problem solving
description: As part of a university course, (Advanced R)", I wrote several scripts simulating and solving the Knapsack problem, a common computer science challenge.

title: Simulation of a Train management system
description: Out of pure interest, I built a system for managing trains, trips, departures etc. This was a great and fun project where I got to experiment with lots of interconnected system parts, and arrange them so that they worked well together.

title: Game of Life
description: I implemented Conway's Game of Life, a cellular automata. Basically, a grid of squares that can be either "alive" or "dead". Depending on surrounding squares, each square changes to simulate overpopulation and underpopulation.
